POST /v1/tickets.description: Two steps: the device first creates a conversation of kind `ticket` (POST /v1/conversations, no keys: tickets are not end-to-end encrypted) listing the requester and the people who may handle it, then calls this with that conversation's id. The subject (250 words at most) and description are kept by the server, encrypted at rest. A place that only takes escalations (GET /v1/tickets/intake) cannot be sent to directly. The server picks a handler, starts the TAT clock and notifies them.

request.category: string. Category name for the recipient
request.to_type: string. desk (default) | department | unit | branch | sector
request.to_ref: uuid. The unit when to_type is not desk

response.id: uuid. Same as the ticket's conversation id
response.step: integer. 0 Raised, 1 Assigned, 2 In progress, 3 Resolved, 4 Closed
response.hold: boolean. true while the TAT clock is paused on hold
response.handler: uuid. The person working on it
response.to_type: string. desk | department | unit | branch | sector
response.to_ref: uuid. The unit it was sent to
response.due_at: timestamp. When it is due, counting working hours
response.participant: boolean. In lists: whether I am in the ticket's conversation and can read its sealed thread

errors.400: Unknown priority or recipient, the category does not exist for that recipient, or the conversation was not created first
errors.403: intake_closed: that place only takes tickets escalated from places it chose

tickets.to_ref: uuid. The unit it was sent to

POST /v1/tickets/{id}/act.description: One endpoint for every step. `do` chooses: assign (set handler/assignees), step (move to Raised, Assigned, In progress, Resolved or Closed), hold, resume, escalate (move to another unit, with a reason) and priority. A person cannot work on a ticket they raised, but may close it. Closing a High priority ticket needs approval (flow f5): resolve it first.
POST /v1/tickets/{id}/act.access: a role with the matching Tickets right (Assign & hand over, Solve, Close, ...)

request.do: string, required. assign | step | hold | resume | escalate | priority
request.to_type: string. escalate: department | unit | branch | sector
request.person: uuid. escalate: who takes it there
request.why: string. escalate: reason, up to 300 characters
request.category: string. escalate: the category at the new place

response.id: uuid. Same as the ticket's conversation id
response.step: integer. 0 Raised, 1 Assigned, 2 In progress, 3 Resolved, 4 Closed
response.hold: boolean. true while the TAT clock is paused on hold
response.handler: uuid. The person working on it
response.to_type: string. desk | department | unit | branch | sector
response.to_ref: uuid. The unit it was sent to
response.due_at: timestamp. When it is due, counting working hours
response.participant: boolean. In lists: whether I am in the ticket's conversation and can read its sealed thread

errors.400: Unknown action, nobody chosen, the person is not in the ticket's conversation, or it is not in the state that action needs
errors.403: own_ticket: you raised it so someone else must work on it
errors.409: already_escalated; needs_approval: closing a High priority ticket needs approval

GET /v1/tickets/feedback.description: Closed, rated tickets I worked on (handler or assignee), or that are with a place I head or a place below it. Newest first, a page at a time. The remark is the closing comment.

POST /v1/tickets/{id}/comments.description: Readable by the server for the ticket's participants. Refused once the ticket is closed.

PUT /v1/tickets/{id}/files.summary: Attach a file to a ticket
PUT /v1/tickets/{id}/files.description: The raw bytes of the file are the body (Content-Type application/octet-stream, Content-Length required). Attachments are plain files kept by the server for the people on the ticket; they are not end-to-end encrypted. Listed in GET /v1/tickets/{id} as `files`.
PUT /v1/tickets/{id}/files.access: Tickets: View, and on the ticket

query.name: the file name, required, up to 255 characters
query.type: its media type; types that could run script are stored as application/octet-stream

GET /v1/tickets/{id}/files/{file}.description: Streams the file as a download, with its safe type and nosniff.
GET /v1/tickets/{id}/files/{file}.access: Tickets: View, and on the ticket

POST /v1/tickets/{id}/chase.summary: Escalate an overdue ticket to the head
POST /v1/tickets/{id}/chase.description: Not the usual escalation: the ticket stays where it is, with the same handler. The note goes to the head of the place it was sent to (the chosen head, else whoever holds that place's head role), who is put on the ticket. The event and the note (as a comment) are recorded. GET /v1/tickets/{id} says can_chase.
POST /v1/tickets/{id}/chase.access: while overdue: the person who raised it, or the head of the place it came from (origin_ref: the dashboard it was sent from, else the raiser's own place)

body.note: required, what the head should know

errors.403: not_allowed: not the raiser or a head of where it came from, or not overdue
errors.409: no_head: the place it was sent to has no head yet

GET /v1/tickets/intake.description: A place listed here is not offered for new tickets or business requests; only members of the places it chose may escalate to it. One row per chosen place.

PUT /v1/tickets/intake.summary: Choose who can send to a place
PUT /v1/tickets/intake.description: Replaces the list of places a place takes escalations from. An empty list opens it to anyone again.
PUT /v1/tickets/intake.access: the head of the place, or Tickets: Set up ticket categories

body.only_from: [uuid], the places it takes escalations from
